name: United Kingdom
key_conventions: Often around 2 pages long; sometimes longer for senior or academic roles
Typically no photo, date of birth, marital status, or National Insurance number included
Reverse-chronological format (most recent role first) is the most common structure
A personal or supporting statement addressing the job description directly is often expected for public-sector roles, especially NHS and Civil Service applications
regulatory_considerations: UK equality law discourages employers from requesting information like age, marital status, or a photo, so many candidates choose not to include this on their CV
Right-to-work status is usually confirmed separately during the recruitment process, not necessarily stated on the CV itself
terminology_notes: 'Personal statement' or 'supporting statement' rather than 'summary', particularly in public-sector applications
source_note: General conventions only, based on common UK recruitment practice — individual employers and sectors vary, and the job description or application instructions should always take priority.
